However, the complainant in para No. 6 of his complaint has averred and extracted the para No. 17 of the agreement as follows:
"in the event committing a breach of any of the terms hereof Or preferring to terminate this agreement for unforeseen circumstances by the vendor, the vendor has issued 3 cheque bearing No.(1) 115349 drawn on ICICI Bank (2) 000032 drawn on HDFC Bank (3) 184536 drawn on State Bank of India in favour of the purchasers for a total amount of Rs.10,20,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Crores Twenty Lakhs only) and the said cheque shall be honoured accordingly without fail until such time for realization of that cheque the PURCHASERS shall have lien on the SCHEDULE PROPERTY as absolute owners"

On going through the said recital it is crystal clear that the Ex.P1, 2 and 3 cheques were alleged to have been issued by the accused, her husband and her son collectively in favour of the complainant for total sum of Rs.
- 25 - C.C.No. 20726/2022 10,20,00,000/- showing collective liability to repay the advance amount if they fail to execute the sale deed as per terms of the agreement.
Such being the case the complainant has presented only cheque of the accused for total sum of Rs. 10,20,00,000/- which is a huge sum.

20. That apart, in the background of such recital as per the complainant, how did the complainant happened to present only the cheque of the accused leaving the cheques of her husband and son to the total value of Rs. 10,20,00,000/- is not explained.
Whether the accused instructed the complainant to do so is not explained.
As discussed above in the presence of Ex.D6 whether accused instructed the complainant to present her cheque for said sum is not explained at all by the complainant.
Three cheques value is written in one cheque.

The complainant has failed to explain in the presence of the recital mentioned above and in the presence of direct reluctance by the accused made in Ex.D6 upon what and whose instructions - 26 - C.C.No. 20726/2022 he presented the Ex.P1 cheque which was issued for the part of the sum of Rs.10,20,00,000/-.

Since above cheque belongs to the accused's account and bears her signature and as the complainant was the holder in due course, the complainant is benefited to raise presumption under Sec.118 and 139 of - 14 - C.C.No. 20726/2022 N.I. Act.

10. Now the burden shifts on the accused to rebut the presumption under Sec.118 and 139 of N.I Act from the defence points either by giving a standard proof or by establishing the same under the principles of preponderance of probabilities.
